oc_definitions.name: Hobbyist / Opportunistic
oc_definitions.description: Single individual with limited expertise, spray-and-pray attacks

oc_definitions.name: Professional Opportunistic
oc_definitions.description: Single professional with broad security capabilities, personal infrastructure

oc_definitions.name: Criminal Syndicates / Insider Threats
oc_definitions.description: Well-resourced criminal groups, disgruntled employees, industrial espionage

oc_definitions.name: Leading Cyber-Capable Nation-States
oc_definitions.description: Foreign intelligence agencies, state-sponsored groups executing 100+ operations annually

oc_definitions.name: Top-Priority State Operations
oc_definitions.description: Highest-priority operations by world's most capable nations, years-ahead-of-public expertise

sl_definitions.name: Basic Controls
sl_definitions.description: Sensitive data internal, basic access control, cloud provider defaults

sl_definitions.name: Professional Best Practices
sl_definitions.description: Centralized weight storage, encrypted transit, FIDO keys, red-teaming, bug bounty

sl_definitions.name: Aggressive Attack Surface Reduction
sl_definitions.description: Copy-resistant interfaces, multiparty auth, insider threat program, advanced red-teaming

sl_definitions.name: Nation-State Defense
sl_definitions.description: Hardware-enforced controls, confidential computing, TEMPEST isolation, zero-day search capability

sl_definitions.name: Top-Priority State Operations Defense
sl_definitions.description: Complete isolation, formal hardware verification, supervised access

defense_layers.name: Physical Perimeter
defense_layers.description: SCIF construction, mantraps, intrusion detection, armed response
defense_layers.independence_notes: Independent from digital layers; correlates with personnel if same guards manage both

defense_layers.name: Network Boundary
defense_layers.description: Air gap, encryptors, bandwidth limits, data diodes, PDS
defense_layers.independence_notes: Independent from physical if network hardware is distinct from perimeter systems

defense_layers.name: Host/OS Security
defense_layers.description: Secure boot, signed code, patch management, endpoint monitoring
defense_layers.independence_notes: Correlates with network_boundary if same vendor provides both; correlates with accelerator_security via driver

defense_layers.name: Accelerator Hardware Security
defense_layers.description: Root-of-trust, memory isolation, interconnect encryption, TEE, tamper protection
defense_layers.independence_notes: Independent from host if accelerator denies host access (device-controlled isolation). Correlates with host via firmware update path.

defense_layers.name: Access Control & Authorization
defense_layers.description: SenL framework, dual authorization, least privilege, key management
defense_layers.independence_notes: Correlates with personnel_trust (same people being vetted and authorized)

defense_layers.name: Monitoring & Detection
defense_layers.description: Behavioral analytics, anomaly detection, audit logs, SOC
defense_layers.independence_notes: Independent from preventive layers; correlates if monitoring system runs on same infrastructure being monitored

defense_layers.name: Personnel Trust & Integrity
defense_layers.description: Vetting, TPI, post-employment controls, insider threat program
defense_layers.independence_notes: Independent from technical layers; correlates with access_control (same people)

defense_layers.name: Supply Chain Integrity
defense_layers.description: Vendor diversity, inspection, provenance, sub-tier flow-down
defense_layers.independence_notes: Independent from operational layers; correlates with accelerator_security if same vendor for both chip and inspection

ai_advancement_timeline.label: AI Advancement Timeline
ai_advancement_timeline.effect: Shifts the AI capability curve earlier (optimistic) or later (pessimistic). At 0: pessimistic_multiplier applied. At 1: optimistic_multiplier applied. At 0.5: default curve.

government_cooperation.label: Government Cooperation
government_cooperation.effect: Increases feasibility and reduces time_to_deploy for blocks requiring government involvement. Unlocks certain blocks entirely at high values.

vendor_cooperation.label: Vendor Cooperation
vendor_cooperation.effect: Reduces time_to_deploy and increases availability of vendor-dependent hardware blocks.

annual_security_budget.label: Annual Security Budget
annual_security_budget.effect: Constrains how many blocks can be invested in simultaneously. Higher budget = more parallel investment. Low budget forces sequencing.

organizational_transformation.label: Organizational Transformation Willingness
organizational_transformation.effect: Modifies organizational_readiness scores for all blocks. Low = blocks with cultural barriers take longer and cost more. High = faster cultural adoption.

risk_tolerance.label: Risk Tolerance
risk_tolerance.effect: Shifts uncertainty ranges. Conservative: use worst-case estimates for feasibility, time, cost. Aggressive: use best-case.

exfiltration_consequences: Safety guardrails removed — unrestricted dangerous capabilities released
Fine-tuning for offensive cyber, biological/chemical weapon design, mass manipulation
Years of R&D ($1-10B+) captured instantly by adversary
Military/intelligence applications: autonomous systems, strategic planning
Recursive improvement: stolen model used to accelerate stealing next model
sabotage_consequences: Corrupted research outputs — months of wasted R&D and wrong conclusions
Poisoned model deployed to customers — cascading trust failure
Subtle backdoors in model behavior — undetectable degradation
Destruction of safety alignment work — undermining entire field
stakes.recursive_risk: If automated AI R&D is compromised, an adversary gains recursive self-improvement capability outside any safety framework — potentially the highest-stakes scenario in the threat model.
